newsitem.title: CANADA: BioChem Pharma falls on Q4 profit results.
newsitem.headline: BioChem Pharma falls on Q4 profit results.

text.p: Shares of BioChem Pharma Inc fell on Thursday on disappointment with the AIDS-drug maker's operating earnings, which were reported on Wednesday, analysts said.
On the Toronto Stock Exchange, BioChem Pharma shares were off C$8.10 to trade at C$70.50 on Thursday afternoon. On the Nasdaq, BioChem was off US$5.50 to trade at US$51.63.

Analysts said that despite surging fourth-quarter net profits on royalties from strong sales of its AIDS drug 3TC, which is marketed as Epivir, the Montreal-based biotechnology company's operating earnings were disappointing.

On Wednesday, BioChem Pharma reported a fourth-quarter net profit of C$19.9 million or C$0.38 a share, compared with C$3.5 million or C$0.08 a share a year earlier. The net profit in the latest quarter came after a C$2 million tax gain and a C$5.5 million gain on share dilution regarding its holding in North American Vaccine Inc.
On an operating basis, BioChem Pharma earned C$12.2 million in the latest quarter, compared with C$4.9 million a year earlier.
"They earned C$12 million on an operating basis, while we were expecting C$18 million," said an analyst who declined to be identified.

The analyst said that while BioChem Pharma's operating profits were disappointing, royalties from sales of 3TC, which is licensed exclusively to Glaxo Wellcome Plc, were stronger than expected in the fourth quarter.

Looking ahead, analysts will watch for results expected to be released at a conference in London in April on the clinical testing of BioChem Pharma's lamivudine drug, a different formulation of 3TC for use in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B.
